messages:
marta: FYI — canary migration v2 applied to prod-canary but we're seeing sustained read-replica lag on replica-3 :eyes:
ashwin: saw that, metrics dashboard shows ~120s lag after the index apply completed
deploy-bot: Deploy started by @marta at 2026-03-21T13:02:47Z 
deploy-bot: Step: online-index-apply v2 -> finished on canary nodes
sre-oncall: 120s is concerning for write-heavy tables. what's the query causing it?
db-eng: looks like the concurrent index build kicked off an async scan that expanded replication WAL bursts. extracting slow queries now
db-eng: snippet of psql check:
```
SELECT pid, state, query_start, query FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE query LIKE '%CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY%';
```
julie: we have a preflight that should have limited to 2 concurrent builds but canary scaling may have bypassed it
ashwin: @@marta did you pin the service version for canary traffic? if canary autoscaled it could've increased replica pressure
marta: I pinned the service to v2-canary briefly but autoscale popped due to a spike. I rolled traffic back to 10% after noticing lag
kevin: proposal: pause remaining canaries, run replica catchup job, then re-run index with throttled maintenance_work_mem + checkpoint_timeout adjustments
sre-oncall: agree. also we should extend the DB migration window by 30 minutes in case catchup takes longer
db-eng: catchup job command (runs on leader only):
```
pg_basebackup -h replica-3 -D /var/lib/pg/catchup --progress && pg_ctl restart -D /var/lib/pg/pgdata
```
(we'll use rsync streaming snapshot for minimal downtime)
ashwin: also adding a small registry flag to release notes so SRE knows this migration touched replica WAL paths: https://internal.redwood/releases/2026-03-schema-v2-notes
ashwin: update: I've created a temporary feature-flag `migration_safe_mode=true` to keep background workers at low concurrency during the window
marta: rolling hold on remaining canaries now. deploy-bot, cancel the staged jobs -> `deploy-bot cancel 7101234601`
deploy-bot: Cancel acknowledged for staged jobs by @marta.
kevin: I'll own the catchup run and confirm lag < 5s before we continue. If not, rollback plan B: revert index apply and restore snapshot to pre-change checkpoint
julie: add a release-note bullet: "Index v2 applied to canary; paused after replica lag observed. Catchup job underway; target resume in 30-60m."
ashwin: tagging #incidents in case proactive paging needed :rotating_light:
sre-oncall: thanks — I'll watch the alerts and escalate if latency spikes beyond 1.5x threshold
marta: once kevin confirms <5s we'll resume with 1% traffic canary and baked in throttling. everyone ok? :thumbsup:
kevin: on it, will post completion or rollback decision in this thread
marta: thanks. adding note to release docs and marking this deploy as "holdpoint: replica-catchup"
kevin: catchup done. replica-3 lag at 3s after streaming rsync and restart. ready to continue at 1% traffic
ashwin: resuming with 1% and concurrency cap set to 2. watching logs for WAL bursts
ashwin: update 15m: stable, pursing normal ramp. will add postmortem line in release notes about autoscale interaction
marta: closing holdpoint. will follow up with a short postmortem and tweak our preflight to block autoscale during index apply. thanks all!
